18746823_c7a36156.section: CA2 as a Distinct Glutamatergic Population

18746823_20361c77.text: CA2 cells recorded from the age group of 11-21-day-old rats and mice are reported to have larger leak currents and more negative resting membrane potentials than CA1 neurons, and stronger current injection is required to evoke their action potentials (Antonio et al., 2014).
18746823_20361c77.section: CA2 as a Distinct Glutamatergic Population

18746823_614030d2.text: Here we report identification of the CA2 region in the mouse by immunostaining with a Purkinje cell protein 4 (PCP4) antibody, which effectively delineates CA3/CA2 and CA2/CA1 borders and agrees well with previous cytoarchitectural definitions of CA2

18746823_fd8665d7.text: our quantification indicates that the average somatic sizes of intracellularly labeled pyramidal cells differ across these regions; the least to greatest average somatic size is CA1<CA2<CA3 (Fig. 8D; Kruskal-Wallis test: P 5 0.002, Mann-Whitney U-tests for group comparisons: CA3 versus CA2 P 5 0.02, CA3 versus CA1 P 5 0.002, CA2 versus CA1 P 5 0.045). In comparison with CA3 cells, both CA2 and CA1 excitatory cells tended to have fewer primary apical branches and more distant branching points (Fig. 8E,F).

18746823_437ba8b3.text: Wherease excitatory pyramidal cells in CA3 had complex postsynaptic spines termed thorny excrescences in their proximal dendrites (Fig. 7J,M,N), CA2 excitatory cells, like CA1 cells, had dense dendritic spines, but did not have such thorny excrescences (Fig. 7K,L,O).
